Town of Pamelia Court

Address: 25859 NY-37, Watertown, NY 13601, United States

Phone: 315-785-9794

Fax: 315-788-0789

Email: sfields@nycourts.gov

Google Maps: 25859 NY-37, Watertown, NY 13601

2. Working Hours

Administrative Hours:

  • Monday to Thursday: 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM

Court Hours:

  • Thursday: 7:00 PM

Closed on Saturdays and Sundays

3. Court Divisions and Jurisdiction

The Town of Pamelia Court operates within the 4th and 5th Judicial District Departments in Jefferson County, New York. It handles:

  • Criminal Division: Cases such as theft, murder, and kidnapping.
  • Civil Division: Disputes between individuals or organizations.
  • Traffic and Vehicle Division: Violations including speeding, reckless driving, and driving under the influence.
  • Small Claims Division: Claims up to $10,000.

Eligibility: Residents and individuals involved in legal issues within the Town of Pamelia.

4. Accessing Court Records

Methods to Search Records:

  • By name
  • By case number
  • By address
  • By phone
  • By email

Confidential Records: Some records are confidential and require a formal open record request to the clerk’s office. Fill out the request form and submit it for approval.

5. Traffic Violation Points System

Traffic violation points vary by infraction. Examples:

  • Speeding: 4 points for exceeding the limit by 11-20 mph; 11 points for exceeding by 40+ mph.
  • Reckless Driving or Using a Cell Phone While Driving: 5 points.
  • Failure to Stop for a School Bus: 5 points.
  • Failure to Yield or Use Proper Child Restraints: 3 points.

Accruing excessive points may lead to license suspension or cancellation.

6. Payment Methods

Payments for tickets or fines can be made via:

  • In-Person: Cash, checks, or credit cards (2.99% service charge applies).
  • Online: Through the court’s payment portal (processing fees apply).
  • Mail: Send a certified check or money order to:
    25859 NY-37, Watertown, NY 13601
    Note: Do not send cash or personal checks.

7. Traffic Division Cases

The traffic division handles:

  • Speeding tickets
  • Moving violations
  • Reckless driving
  • Criminal traffic offenses (e.g., DUI)
  • Accidents and failure to obey traffic control devices

In some cases, submitting a plea (guilty or not guilty) is sufficient, while others may require court appearance.

8. Court Appearance Requirements

  • Criminal Cases: Mandatory appearance.
  • Traffic Cases: Submit a plea. The court will notify if appearance is required.

9. Criminal Division Cases

Criminal cases include serious offenses like murder, theft, and drug-related crimes. Hiring an attorney is mandatory for legal representation.

10. Small Claims Division Cases

The small claims division resolves claims up to $10,000. Key points:

  • Court fee: $30
  • Attorney: Not required
  • Eligibility: Plaintiff must be 18+ and located in the town.

11. Obtaining a Marriage License

Marriage licenses are issued by the Town Clerk’s Office. Requirements:

  • Fee: $40 (certificates cost $10 each)
  • Age: Both parties must be 18+. Parental consent is required for individuals aged 16-17. Superior court approval is mandatory for those under 16.
  • Documents: Birth certificate and photo ID (e.g., passport, driver’s license).

Application Process:

  • Fill out the marriage form.
  • Submit necessary documentation.
  • Attend the court for a ceremony (if applicable).

12. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q: How can I pay for a traffic ticket? A: Payments can be made online, by mail, or in person.

Q: What licenses or certificates does the clerk’s office provide? A: Marriage licenses, birth certificates, and death certificates.

Q: What are the courtroom etiquettes? A:

  • No electronic devices, food, or weapons are allowed.
  • Dress appropriately; hats and sunglasses must be removed.
  • Recording or speaking during proceedings is prohibited.

For more information, contact Sheri Fields, Court Clerk, at sfields@nycourts.gov.
